decisions.reason: The dismantling joint is a natural complement to the firm's core fittings for water infrastructure, costs almost nothing to keep listed, and serves steady utility demand, so the option remains worth holding.

The ceiling or floor bracket uses existing steel and stainless fabrication at low marginal cost and complements pipeline installation projects, so there is no evidence that would justify abandoning it.
The pipe support bracket is closely tied to the firm's pipeline component business and is cheap to keep, so it remains a low-cost option with plausible ongoing demand.

The public waste bin is distant from the core business, but it uses the firm's powder-coating equipment and reaches the same municipal customers, so the cost of carrying it is modest while its value is still uncertain.

The waste bin with ashtray is a multi-model line outside the core business and costs more to maintain, but municipal sales cycles are slow and three years is too little to show its value is unlikely, so the option stays open.

The outdoor ashtrays have the weakest fit and face declining smoking-related demand, which raises the risk of abandonment, but they share coating capacity and customers with the bins, so the firm would likely keep the street-furniture options together for now.
